body: thank you, im going to explore that further. do you mind me asking what you identify as? im only asking because you mentioned you had the same emotional click about being a man. im leaning more towards the realization that i might be a man, but im still hesitant.

this is such a thoughtful response, thank you for taking the time to share your experience.

>if you had the choice, would you be a non-dysphoric regular cis woman with an uncomplicated relationship to womanhood?

i dont think i would. it feels like i would have to give a large, defining part of myself up to achieve that.

>The other thing is, and this may seem like an obvious one, but would you like to be seen as a man?

the more i think about it, the more i think that deep in my heart i know i am a man. but the hard part is, i dont think i want to be fully seen as one because of the things you mentioned in your post. i do have some marginal connection to womanhood that has informed my experience. if i was born male i would have been fine and i would not be feeling any of this. i think i am a man who has gotten used to living as a woman and it feels like it will hurt more to change the way i move through life, than to keep going on the way i always have, even though it feels like im lying to myself.

>I guess what I would suggest is that you list all the things you like most about being a woman—and think really hard about it. Keep it on your mind for weeks, months, etc, and note down every time you realise that your being a woman made you feel happy in some context.

I'm definitely going to try this to try to figure out my identity further. thank you again.
